headline: Two hours with Putin. Then a plane to Zelensky.
summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin for about two hours on Thursday, then flew to Dublin to see Volodymyr Zelensky. Two days of Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi had ended with a prisoner swap and no breakthrough. Putin told the envoys any European troops in Ukraine after a ceasefire would be targets.

cover_question.q: Why not put them in one room?

cover_answer: They tried that for two days. It got a prisoner swap.
table_question: Two friends are fighting. Talk to them together, or one at a time?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Two American helpers flew to Russia today and talked to its leader for two hours, then flew to Ireland to talk to Ukraine's leader. Russia and Ukraine have been at war for almost five years. The helpers go back and forth like a grown-up walking between two kids who won't talk. The war is far away, and the grown-ups keep trying.
5-7.why: A six-year-old knows the walk between two kids who won't talk. That is the whole story at this age.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and a war is not. A grown-up walking between two kids who won't talk is: they have seen it at recess. The script gives them two plane rides and a count of hours, and keeps the fighting far away. Expect 'did they make up?' Not yet. The grown-ups are still going back and forth.

8-12.script: Russia and Ukraine sat in one room in Abu Dhabi for two days, their first direct talks in nine months. They agreed on a prisoner swap and little else. So the Americans running the talks saw Putin for two hours, then flew to Zelensky: a referee pulling each captain aside.
8-12.why: A chain to follow: one room, two days, a swap, then one leader at a time.
8-12.why_long: At ten they are working out chains of cause and effect, so the script hands them one: a shared room for two days produced a prisoner swap and nothing else, so the envoys went to each leader alone. The referee pulling a captain aside is a mechanism they know. Expect 'who is winning?' Neither side has given up what the other wants.

13-17.script: Should Europe be in the room when the talks are about its own security? The US ran two days of Russia-Ukraine talks with no European present. Russia says no. Second: the US waived sanctions on Russia last month and made a deal for its diesel. Can it still referee?
13-17.why: Two true things: America is the broker, and it leans Russia's way.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the US is the only party talking to both sides, and it has waived sanctions and made a diesel deal with one of them. The script adds Europe's claim to a seat and Russia's refusal. Expect 'is America on Russia's side?' Both facts stand; they decide what one does to the other.

5-7.a: Not yet. The talking keeps going, and talking is how wars end. It is a long way from here.

8-12.q: Why not put them in one room?
8-12.a: They did, for two days in Abu Dhabi. It got a prisoner swap and no more.
Each side sends home soldiers it captured. The number is not out yet.

13-17.q: Why does Russia want Europe kept out?
13-17.a: Russia says Europe pays for and arms Ukraine's army. So no seat.
Trump waived sanctions last month and made a diesel deal. You decide.
